stem: A kidney recipient with a recent surgical wound asks about starting sirolimus. Which counseling point aligns with standard medication references?

options.text: Sirolimus may impair wound healing, so initiation may be delayed in some clinical situations
Sirolimus accelerates wound healing and should always start immediately after surgery
Sirolimus has no effect on wound healing or graft recovery
Sirolimus is the preferred agent during active wound dehiscence

explanation.rationale_correct: Sirolimus has been associated with impaired wound healing and delay in renal allograft recovery; delaying initiation may be warranted in these clinical situations.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sirolimus may impair rather than accelerate wound healing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Wound-healing impairment is a recognized sirolimus concern requiring clinical judgment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Active wound problems may warrant delaying sirolimus rather than preferential use.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Pharmacology → Sirolimus → dosing notes → v.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: associated with impaired wound healing and delay in renal allograft recovery … delaying the initiation of sirolimus may be warranted

stem: When coordinating post-transplant health maintenance for a solid-organ recipient, when do most centers restart vaccinations per standard references?

options.text: Only after 10 years of stable graft function
Immediately in the recovery room before discharge
Vaccinations are never restarted after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Although the ideal post-transplant vaccination timing is unknown, most centers restart vaccinations approximately 3 to 6 months after transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Vaccination restart occurs much earlier than a 10-year interval in most programs.
rationale_incorrect.C: Most centers defer vaccination restart for several months rather than administering vaccines in the recovery room.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant vaccination restart is recommended rather than permanently avoided.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: most centers restart vaccinations approximately 3 to 6 months posttransplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

stem: A kidney transplant recipient with rising creatinine has confirmed BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy. Which complication pattern aligns with standard references?

options.text: Tubulointerstitial nephritis with possible ureteral stenosis and progressive graft dysfunction
Isolated cosmetic skin rash without renal involvement
Expected benign finding that never threatens graft function
Primary graft tenderness as the hallmark manifestation

explanation.rationale_correct: BK virus reactivation may cause tubulointerstitial nephritis, ureteral stenosis leading to obstructive nephropathy, progressive graft dysfunction, and graft loss in polyomavirus-associated nephropathy.

rationale_incorrect.B: BK nephropathy causes renal tubular and ureteral complications rather than isolated skin findings.
rationale_incorrect.C: BK-associated nephropathy may cause significant morbidity and graft dysfunction.
rationale_incorrect.D: Graft tenderness is not the hallmark of BK nephropathy; renal dysfunction and tubulointerstitial injury predominate.

stem: A kidney transplant recipient has rising BK viral replication on surveillance testing. Evaluate the following risk and complication statements:

elements.text: Intense immunosuppression is a modulating risk factor for BK virus reactivation.
Ureteric stents are a post-transplant modulating factor associated with BK risk.
BK and JC viruses never reactivate in immunosuppressed transplant recipients.
BK reactivation may cause ureteral stenosis leading to obstructive nephropathy.

explanation.rationale_correct: BK risk is increased by intense immunosuppression and ureteric stents and may cause ureteral stenosis with obstructive nephropathy. Statement III is false because BK and JC viruses often reactivate in immunosuppressed recipients.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—ureteral stenosis with obstructive nephropathy is a listed complication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false—polyomaviruses often reactivate in immunosuppressed recipients.
